triggers.desc: Triggers run this custom agent automatically. Each trigger creates and runs a new session, visible on the Conversations page. Select multiple trigger conditions if needed. The system appends the trigger reason and related task, finding, or goal to your default message.
triggers.policyLabel: Post-trigger processing policy (determining how to queue and merge and execute the trigger)
triggers.serial: Serial (in the queue, one at a time)
triggers.policyParallel: Parallel: Whenever triggered, you immediately open a session one at a time to run it at the same time, and you don't merge. Triggers that exceed maximum concurrent execution enter the queue, waiting for a blank spot.
triggers.policyByTask: Merge by Serial and Work: The same agent executes only one at a time, and merges the event triggers of the same task into a session in a queue.
triggers.policyAll: Merge Serials and All: The same agent executes only one at a time, and when you pull out a queue, you merge all currently pending triggers into one session.
triggers.policyNone: Do not serially merge: The same agent executes only one at a time, and each trigger opens one session.

trafficCapture.title: Traffic capture
trafficCapture.desc:
When enabled, all agent HTTP traffic is saved through the recording proxy. Agents receive traffic_search / traffic_get tools and proxy settings, including proxy instructions in their prompts.

When disabled (the default), no traffic is recorded. Agents do not receive proxy settings or traffic tools, and their prompts do not include proxy instructions. Changing this setting recreates agents immediately.
trafficCapture.on: On · recording traffic and injecting proxies
trafficCapture.off: No off, no recording, no proxy injection

agentBinding.title: Agent automatic traffic connection
agentBinding.desc:
Disabled by default. When enabled, the report agent compares existing HTTP requests and responses, links matching traffic, and writes the report. Looking up packets and calling additional tools increases token usage.

Reporting still works for TCP, uncaptured packets, or unmatched traffic. This does not affect traffic capture, manual linking, or viewing stored evidence. It applies to the next agent run; disabling immediately rejects new automatic links.
agentBinding.off: Off · Manual connection is still possible

globalProxy.title: Global Proxy
globalProxy.desc:
All agents' target traffic passes through this proxy (using a relay or concealing the source IP). Supports http / https / socks5 with optional user:pass authentication. Leave blank for direct connections.

With traffic capture enabled, this proxy is upstream of the recording proxy: traffic is still saved before forwarding. With capture disabled, settings are injected into agents' bash / WebFetch environments. Web search and LLM proxies are independent.

Note: socks5 with capture disabled depends on each command-line tool honoring ALL_PROXY. curl supports it, but some tools may ignore it. Enabling capture provides a more reliable socks5 route because the MITM proxy establishes the connection itself.
globalProxy.configured: Set up · All target traffic goes out to this proxy
globalProxy.notConfigured: Not set · Target traffic goes directly to the connection

constraints.title: Motion Pharmaceutical Injection
constraints.desc:
When enabled, a task's operation constraints (allow/deny entries managed in its overview) are appended to the agent's system prompt to limit exploration, such as testing only the current port or prohibiting brute force.

Control injection independently for the planner and worker; both are enabled by default. Changes apply on the next round without recreating agents. Disabling removes those constraints from that agent's prompt.

experimental.title: Experimental function
experimental.desc:
Features still under validation, disabled by default. Review their effects before enabling them because they may affect agent behavior or stability.

noa context compression: the model compresses long conversation histories directly (norma v0.4.0). The four supported agent types (planner / worker / main agent / chat) use noa instead of built-in compression. Originals are stored in the task's working directory for review. Changes apply to subsequent runs without recreating agents. Disabling restores built-in compression immediately.

webSearch.title: Web search
webSearch.desc:
Web search master switch and source settings. Enable it before selecting web_search in each agent's settings. Search returns titles, links, and summaries; WebFetch retrieves page bodies. Search bypasses the recording proxy and is independent of traffic capture.

Choose DuckDuckGo (ddgs) (no key), Brave (free tier) (Brave API key), Tavily (Tavily API key), or DeepSeek (reuses current LLM settings). Disabling the master switch prevents individual agents from enabling search.

webSearch.deepseekDesc2: Unlike other sources, the DeepSeek server executes searches. Each search uses an additional model call and incurs token costs. Requests bypass the exit proxy above and are not included in traffic recordings. Results contain only titles and links, without summaries. WebFetch retrieves bodies when needed.

pool.desc: When turned on, when the agent who did not specify the model is unable to write the current settings (lack of balance / Key expiration / call limit / service error), it will automatically switch to the following settings:

enable.label: Circulation
enable.hint: The default is Off. If it is off, it always uses only active settings, and if it fails, it fails.

bindFallback.label: Even if the designating model fails, Fallback
bindFallback.hint: The default is Off: If an agent or task sets a specific setting, it will only use that setting, and if it fails, it will fail (not secretly change to another model). When on, it will fall into the following circulation chain when the specified setting fails.

order.label: Circulating order
order.tooFew: There are only {n} of settings that can be used at the moment, so the circulation does not work. You need at least two settings to fill in the API Key and join the cycle.

recoverNow.title: Instant recovery: Unblock the circuit and try this setting again in the next call

pool.note: The active settings are always first-priority, with the rest being in high-priority order (specified by each setting). If any setting fails, it goes into a cooldown (60s → 5min → 30min), skips during a cooldown, and automatically re-in-re-enleaves when the current request is recovered. Skips the settings that do not currently enter the context window. The agent and task that you specified for the model do not participate in the cycle by default.

profile.descNew: Newly created and it will not be activated automatically. Press "Set to Active" on the card. Use it.

proxy.label: Proxy (optional)
proxy.hint: Only the LLM outbound request goes through this proxy. It supports http/https/socks5 and can include accounts and passwords (e.g. socks5://user:pass@host:port, URL encoding if the password has a special character). If left blank, you do not use the proxy (direct connection).

sessionHeader.label: Custom Session Header (Select)
sessionHeader.placeholder: Example: x-session-id (does not send if empty)
sessionHeader.hint: Set a header name to send this HTTP header on every request. Its value is automatically set to the current session ID, such as conv-12 for chat or exp3-worker-i87 for workers. Use it for prompt caching or sticky routing in a gateway. The value is stable across turns within a session and differs between sessions. Leave blank to omit it.

profile.rateHint: Speed limit 0 = Unlimited, shared by all agents. The context window unit is K (Cenize token), 0 = Default 200K, and the upper limit 1000 (i.e. 1M). If you hold it too large, compression is not triggered.

priority.label: Circulating priorities
priority.hint: The larger the number, the first choice. The active setting is always the first priority, regardless of this value. The priority setting alternates in front of you and naturally divides the quota.

exclude.label: Excluding Circulation
exclude.hint: If you turn it on, you will not be eligible for a disabled conversion (you can still use it if you explicitly specify an agent or task). It is suitable for expensive settings that you want to "prevent when others fail because it is only for certain agents".

streaming.label: Streaming Output · Streaming
streaming.hint: When turned on (default), it will run as a streaming SSE to see the real-time progress and the number of real-time tokens during execution. When turned off, it will run as real-time non-streaming (returning the completed response at once) to bypass the bad SSE implementation of some gateways (empty frames/accident field missing frames), but it loses real-time progress during execution.

maxTokens.label: Output cap · max tokens
maxTokens.hint: Create up to a few tokens in one response, send them together on each request. 0 (default) = Follow the server default without sending this field. This is different from the "context window" above. It is used only when calculating the compression threshold locally, with the full capacity of the model. If you hold it too small, the inference model will not answer even one letter that was cut in the accident stage.

maxTokensFieldHint.openai: The upper limit is the key to which it is sent. max_tokens are the default and most compatible gateways recognize this, whereas the OpenAI official inference model (o series / GPT-5) recognizes only max_completion_tokens, and gives an unsupported_parameter error as soon as you receive max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.anthropic: You can only choose from the openai format. The field name of Anthropic is fixed to max_tokens.
maxTokensFieldHint.openai-responses: You can only choose from the openai format. The field name of the Responses API is fixed to max_output_tokens.

thinkingType.label: Thinking.type
thinkingType.hint: Controls whether to send the thinking field. Do not send = send without this field (compatible with models that do not support MiniMax, etc.); Off=disabled send; On=enabled send. The intensity below is independent of each other.

effort.label: Accident Strength · reasoning_effort
effort.hint: Independent intensity stage (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Anthropic output_config.effort). Some interfaces do not have a thinking field and can turn on the incident only with strength, so you can set the intensity separately without sending an accident switch.

connect.title: Retend connection
connect.trigger: If not connected or not yet received 200: Network layer errors such as connection reset / read/write timeout / DNS failure, and HTTP 408·429·500·502·503·504.
connect.skips: The other status code (400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 413 / 422, etc.) is a definite rejection, and it fails to do the same, so it is raised immediately.
connect.desc: Sends the same request back as it is. Once the stream is started (already receiving 200s), this layer is not responsible for it if it is broken.
connect.offHint: -1 = Never retreact and immediately lift the failure up

empty.title: Re-tries empty response
empty.trigger: If it is HTTP 200 and finish_reason is a normal stop, but there is no content block in the entire response. Gateway empty frames, missed thought fields, and sampling hiccups all appear like this.
empty.skips: Except if you have no content cut with max_tokens (it needs to be solved by raising the output limit, and if you send it back, it will hit the same wall again).
empty.desc: Since the full prompt is sent back, it is better not to take the number of times because the cost is large in a long context.
empty.offHint: -1 = Send an empty response as it is

stream.title: Re-tries for the same provider safety section
stream.trigger: The problem with the stream after it has already been established (200 received): disconnection during the process, provider overloaded, 429 / 5xx error event inside the stream, and has not yet passed any token to the caller.
stream.skips: Quota burnout (402 / insufficient_quota, cyclical changes settings), over-contacular (413 / context length, compression processed), and 400 / 401 / 403 / 404 / 422 definitive rejections are not retreacted.
stream.desc: Replay the same request again in the same settings. Since no output has been delivered yet, playing does not duplicate the model output or tool execution.
stream.offHint: -1 = When the stream is broken, it is immediately passed to the intention re-run of the outer layer

breaker.title: Circular circuit blocking
breaker.where: This project · process unit, one in the global
breaker.trigger: Block temporary failures (429·5xx·network errors) if they accumulate to the threshold in a row. Confirmed failures such as low balance (402), key expiration (402), and no model (404) block from the beginning without seeing the threshold.
breaker.skips: Once successful, it is initialized to zero, so sometimes trouble-prone settings are not blocked.
breaker.desc: If it is blocked, it enters the cooldown, and during the cooldown, the circulation skips this setting. The state is stored in the DB and will not disappear even if restarted.
breaker.attemptsLabel: Block if it fails a few times in a row
breaker.offHint: -1 = Never block temporary failures (confirmed failures are still blocked)

intent.title: Intent Relaunch
intent.where: This project · process unit, one in the global
intent.trigger: If the previous multiple layers failed to block: the worker ended with model_error. If you have exhausted all the internal retretries, or you have broken it after the stream has already started delivering the output (at that time, the playback is not secure, so you have to run the whole thing again).
intent.skips: Quota burnout does not rerun here, as the circulation already changes the settings, so it will not re-run here. If the task goes into pause/end/finish, it will yield immediately and will not take up the backoff time.
intent.desc: The entire intent is executed from the beginning. It is the outermost layer, and once it is re-executed, the number of layers inside is multiplied once again.
intent.offHint: -1 = determined to block the intention without re-runing it

retry.emptyLine: If left blank, use the default {hint}.

override.label: Re-launch redefining
override.hint: This setting only is applied to this setting to override the global default value of "Residtion and Backoff". When you empty each field, it follows the entire. If you put -1 in the number of times, this layer will be turned off. If you fill in the interval, the fixed interval is used instead of the exponential backoff. Circuit blocking and Intent re-run can only be adjusted on the entire page because it is a process unit.

retry.intro: One failure of the model call goes through five layers of retries in the order from the inside to the outside: <chain>Connection → Empty Response → Same provider safe interval → Circular circuit blocking → Intent re-run</chain>. Since the outer turn comes by using all the inner layers, the number of times <emph>They're multiplying.</emph>. If you raise each floor to the maximum, one shake can burn dozens of requests. If you empty them all, it is the current default, and it is exactly the same as when this page is not there. The first three layers can be overridden separately in each model setting.

ClosedLoop.title: Closed-loop
ClosedLoop.heading: Improve with attack and defense evidence and re-verify with independent data
ClosedLoop.description: Build a candidate rule using tuning logs, then apply baseline and candidate rules to separate labeled attack and benign evaluation logs. Use false negatives, false positives, and missing fields to prioritize the next assessment and collection checks.
ClosedLoop.invalidId: The connection ID must be a positive integer.
ClosedLoop.tooLarge: The file must be less than 2 MiB. The sum of the two datasets must be less than 2 MiB.
ClosedLoop.resultScope: This result is an offline assessment with a small rule applied to the logs that the uploader has displayed as an attack or normal. It does not prove the actual attack success, SIEM alert, or the completion of the deployment.
ClosedLoop.metricLimits: If there is no denominator or missing the required log field, the indicator is not counted. MTTD calculates only when the actual alarm time and attack time for each rule are at all and there is a source confirmation. The results depend on the sample size and label accuracy.
ClosedLoop.priorities: Priority for next attack and defense verification
ClosedLoop.priorityDescription: Based on the events below, plan to reenact attacks, check normal traffic, or supplement log collection. We do not perform automatic attack execution or rule deployment.
ClosedLoop.noPriorities: No counterexamples to the candidate rule in this dataset. Continue validation with new independent data and a real detection environment.
ClosedLoop.label: Ground-truth label
ClosedLoop.tuningResults: View improvement data results · Not the final performance indicator
ClosedLoop.prepareDescription: Prepare two JSONL files with the attack and normal correct answer labels. If the same event ID or same log is entered into the two datasets, the evaluation is rejected.
ClosedLoop.scenarioPlaceholder: Example: Improved detection of internal file access by anonymous users
ClosedLoop.syntheticScenario: Synthetic example: anonymous internal file access rule
ClosedLoop.syntheticNotice: This is synthetic data for demonstrating functionality. It does not demonstrate real attacks or detection improvements.
ClosedLoop.referenceLimits: Vulnerabilities and events are selectively linked. Connections alone do not prove that they are logs from the same attack execution. The original evidence of the connection is preserved as a snapshot when stored and can be found in the export.
ClosedLoop.tuningDescription: Data you use to create candidates. Put the attack and normal events together and give each event a unique ID.
ClosedLoop.evaluationDescription: This is data that has not been used to improve candidates. This file will not be sent to the candidate proposal request. If you have viewed the evaluation and changed the rules, prepare a new independent data.
ClosedLoop.jsonlPlaceholder: One JSON object in a row: event_id, label, fields
ClosedLoop.formatDescription: Set label to attack or benign. Put source log string, number, and boolean fields in fields. Labels and IDs cannot be used as detection conditions. Each dataset allows up to 1,000 events, 64 KiB per line, and 2 MiB for both files combined. Duplicate events with identical fields are rejected even if their label, ID, or time differs.
ClosedLoop.timestampFormat: Time is optional and in RFC3339 format. occurred_at is the actual attack observation time, baseline_alert_at and candidate_alert_at are alarm times that each rule generates in the actual detection environment. Do not enter offline matching time or estimated time.
ClosedLoop.ruleDescription: An event matches if every condition in any one group matches. Only equals (exact match) and contains (substring) are supported. This is not a Sigma, Suricata, or Splunk rule engine. Conditions reference fields inside fields.
ClosedLoop.candidateRule: Candidate rules JSON · Can be edited directly
ClosedLoop.suggest: Suggest a candidate with only a log for improvement
ClosedLoop.suggestDescription: Find exact field values in attacks missed by the baseline and add conditions that do not match benign tuning data. Automatic suggestions can overfit, so review them. You can manually edit rules to address existing false positives.
ClosedLoop.unresolved: Events that have not yet been described as candidates
ClosedLoop.confirmedTimes: Verify that the attack time and the two rule-specific alarm times have been verified in the actual source log and are associated with the same event.
ClosedLoop.previewStale: The input has changed. Compare again and save it.
ClosedLoop.heldOutSameData: The result of applying the reference rules and candidate rules to the same evaluation data.
ClosedLoop.historyDescription: The data, rules, and results stored are not modified, and new comparisons are recorded separately.
ClosedLoop.emptyHistory: There are no saved iterations. Prepare the files, compare them, and save the first result.
ClosedLoop.immutableSnapshot: Rules, label, basis and result at the time of storage. Even if the linked original is modified, this record will not change.
